lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The North Pole Reindeer Training Grounds. Where the Squad comes to sweat, stretch, and settle scores.
lines.spoken: The North Pole Reindeer Training Grounds. --- Where the Squad comes to sweat, stretch, and settle scores.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Floodlights. Fresh snow. A running track that went around and around, like this case.
lines.spoken: Floodlights. -- Fresh snow. ---- A running track that went around and around, like this case.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: And up in the bleachers, a familiar puddle with a familiar voice.
lines.spoken: And up in the bleachers, a familiar puddle with a familiar voice.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Yoo-hoo! Detective! Down here! Well, up here. You're down there.
lines.spoken: Yoo-hoo! - Detective! - Down here! - Well, up here. --- You're down there.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: I brought a thermos and a seat cushion. I'll be watching you work, dear. Closely.
lines.spoken: I brought a thermos and a seat cushion. - I'll be watching you work, dear. --- Closely.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Great. A heckler. Every detective needs one. Mine came with a thermos.
lines.spoken: Great. -- A heckler. -- Every detective needs one. ---- Mine came with a thermos.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Ask better questions! Use your legs! Oh, well. Use what you've got!
lines.spoken: Ask better questions! - Use your legs! - Oh, well. --- Use what you've got!

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Out on the track, Comet was running laps. Every time her hooves hit the snow, the snow said 'tsss.'
lines.spoken: Out on the track, Comet was running laps. --- Every time her hooves hit the snow, the snow said 'tsss.'

lines.speaker: comet
lines.text: Well, look who it is. You following me, sugar?
lines.spoken: Well, look who it is. - You following me, sugar?

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Just doing my rounds. Same as you.
lines.spoken: Just doing my rounds. --- Same as you.

lines.speaker: comet
lines.text: Can't stop, little man. Gotta keep my heart rate up. And my temperature.
lines.spoken: Can't stop, little man. - Gotta keep my heart rate up. --- And my temperature.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: She jogged off in a cloud of steam. A dedicated athlete. You don't see that much anymore.
lines.spoken: She jogged off in a cloud of steam. -- A dedicated athlete. ---- You don't see that much anymore.

lines.speaker: dasher
lines.text: Dasher, fastest in the Squad, and you must be the detective who's here about...
lines.spoken: Dasher, fastest in the Squad, and you must be the detective who's here about ---

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Jimmy Mitt...
lines.spoken: Jimmy Mitt ---

lines.speaker: dasher
lines.text: Jimmy Mittens's taxes, sure, sure, I heard. Terrible business. Numbers. Never liked 'em.
lines.spoken: Jimmy Mittens's taxes, sure, sure, I heard. - Terrible business. - Numbers. --- Never liked 'em.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: No. Jimmy Mittens melted. Where were you last night, between...
lines.spoken: No. -- Jimmy Mittens melted. ---- Where were you last night, between ---

lines.speaker: dasher
lines.text: Between laps? Right here. Running. Ask anyone. Ask the track. The track knows me.
lines.spoken: Between laps? - Right here. - Running. - Ask anyone. - Ask the track. --- The track knows me.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: He finished every sentence before I did, and got every one of them wrong. Either he was hiding something, or he just really liked running.
lines.spoken: He finished every sentence before I did, and got every one of them wrong. --- Either he was hiding something, or he just really liked running.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Through the tinsel goggles, one of the starting blocks lit up. Burnt black. Still smoking a little.
lines.spoken: Through the tinsel goggles, one of the starting blocks lit up. -- Burnt black. ---- Still smoking a little.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Somebody had set fire to it. On purpose? By accident? With their feet?
lines.spoken: Somebody had set fire to it. -- On purpose? -- By accident? ---- With their feet?

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: No. Arson. Professional arson. The kind of fire you only get from two brothers with a grudge.
lines.spoken: No. -- Arson. -- Professional arson. ---- The kind of fire you only get from two brothers with a grudge.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: And I knew just where to find them.
lines.spoken: And I knew just where to find them.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The launch runway was on the far side of the grounds. I could hear the shouting from here.
lines.spoken: The launch runway was on the far side of the grounds. --- I could hear the shouting from here.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The launch runway. A long, icy ramp pointing straight at the sky. Reindeer practice their takeoffs here. Some of them land.
lines.spoken: The launch runway. -- A long, icy ramp pointing straight at the sky. -- Reindeer practice their takeoffs here. ---- Some of them land.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Halfway up the ramp, two reindeer stood nose to nose, yelling about a harness.
lines.spoken: Halfway up the ramp, two reindeer stood nose to nose, yelling about a harness.

lines.speaker: donner
lines.text: That's MY spot! Front left! It's been my spot since 1823!
lines.spoken: That's MY spot! - Front left! --- It's been my spot since 1823!

lines.speaker: blitzen
lines.text: It was never your spot! You stole it! You stole it the night of the poem!
lines.spoken: It was never your spot! - You stole it! --- You stole it the night of the poem!

lines.speaker: donner
lines.text: The poem says Donner! It's right there in the poem!
lines.spoken: The poem says Donner! - It's right there in the poem!

lines.speaker: blitzen
lines.text: Some versions say Donder! Who even is Donder?
lines.spoken: Some versions say Donder! - Who even is Donder?

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Gentlemen. Where were you last night?
lines.spoken: Gentlemen. --- Where were you last night?

lines.speaker: donner
lines.text: Arguing with him.
lines.spoken: Arguing with him.

lines.speaker: blitzen
lines.text: Arguing with him.
lines.spoken: Arguing with him.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Same alibi. Word for word. Very suspicious.
lines.spoken: Same alibi. -- Word for word. ---- Very suspicious.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The harness. Front left. The most fought-over strip of leather at the North Pole.
lines.spoken: The harness. -- Front left. ---- The most fought-over strip of leather at the North Pole.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: And then it hit me. Like a sleigh hitting a chimney.
lines.spoken: And then it hit me. --- Like a sleigh hitting a chimney.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Donner and Blitzen did it. Together. They melted Jimmy as a team-building exercise.
lines.spoken: Donner and Blitzen did it. -- Together. ---- They melted Jimmy as a team-building exercise.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: No. Wait. They did it separately. Each one melted half of Jimmy, so the other one couldn't take the credit. Or the harness.
lines.spoken: No. -- Wait. -- They did it separately. -- Each one melted half of Jimmy, so the other one couldn't take the credit. ---- Or the harness.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: It was brilliant. It was diabolical. It didn't make any sense. That's how I knew I was onto something.
lines.spoken: It was brilliant. -- It was diabolical. -- It didn't make any sense. ---- That's how I knew I was onto something.

lines.speaker: donner
lines.text: Is he okay?
lines.spoken: Is he okay?

lines.speaker: blitzen
lines.text: He's been talking to the harness for a while.
lines.spoken: He's been talking to the harness for a while.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: A good theory needs fuel. I followed the smell of roasted carrots.
lines.spoken: A good theory needs fuel. --- I followed the smell of roasted carrots.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The snack stand. Hot cocoa, roasted carrots, and a menu board I'd need a ladder to read.
lines.spoken: The snack stand. --- Hot cocoa, roasted carrots, and a menu board I'd need a ladder to read.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Leaning on the counter, smooth as butter, was Cupid. Off duty from the lounge. Still smooth.
lines.spoken: Leaning on the counter, smooth as butter, was Cupid. -- Off duty from the lounge. ---- Still smooth.

lines.speaker: cupid
lines.text: Well, if it isn't the little detective. Can I buy you a carrot? Everyone else owes me one.
lines.spoken: Well, if it isn't the little detective. - Can I buy you a carrot? --- Everyone else owes me one.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Everyone?
lines.spoken: Everyone?

lines.speaker: cupid
lines.text: Let me check my ledger. Dasher, two carrots. Donner, seven. Blitzen, seven, but he says it's six.
lines.spoken: Let me check my ledger. - Dasher, two carrots. - Donner, seven. --- Blitzen, seven, but he says it's six.

lines.speaker: cupid
lines.text: And Jimmy Mittens. Fourteen carrots. Never paid.
lines.spoken: And Jimmy Mittens. - Fourteen carrots. --- Never paid.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Fourteen carrots. That's a lot of motive.
lines.spoken: Fourteen carrots. --- That's a lot of motive.

lines.speaker: cupid
lines.text: That's a lot of carrots. And now I'll never see them. Unless the one in that puddle was mine.
lines.spoken: That's a lot of carrots. - And now I'll never see them. --- Unless the one in that puddle was mine.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I studied that ledger the way a detective studies a ledger. Squinting. Nodding. Occasionally turning it upside down.
lines.spoken: I studied that ledger the way a detective studies a ledger. -- Squinting. -- Nodding. ---- Occasionally turning it upside down.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: And the pieces came together. Big pieces. Pieces the size of reindeer.
lines.spoken: And the pieces came together. -- Big pieces. ---- Pieces the size of reindeer.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Everybody owed Cupid carrots. Dasher. Donner. Blitzen. Jimmy. Somebody had to pay. And somebody paid in snowman.
lines.spoken: Everybody owed Cupid carrots. -- Dasher. -- Donner. -- Blitzen. -- Jimmy. -- Somebody had to pay. ---- And somebody paid in snowman.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: This wasn't a murder. It was a carrot cartel. A frozen-vegetable syndicate, run out of a snack stand, with tentacles reaching all the way to the lounge. And possibly the Easter Bunny.
lines.spoken: This wasn't a murder. -- It was a carrot cartel. -- A frozen-vegetable syndicate, run out of a snack stand, with tentacles reaching all the way to the lounge. ---- And possibly the Easter Bunny.

lines.speaker: cupid
lines.text: Do you want the carrot or not?
lines.spoken: Do you want the carrot or not?

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I took the carrot. For evidence.
lines.spoken: I took the carrot. --- For evidence.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Something was nagging at me. Something I'd seen back at the track. Something up high. Something I couldn't reach.
lines.spoken: Something was nagging at me. -- Something I'd seen back at the track. -- Something up high. ---- Something I couldn't reach.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: You've been gone an hour! Did you solve it?
lines.spoken: You've been gone an hour! - Did you solve it?

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I've uncovered a carrot cartel, ma'am.
lines.spoken: I've uncovered a carrot cartel, ma'am.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Oh, honey. You had a snowball's chance in hell of getting that right.
lines.spoken: Oh, honey. - You had a snowball's chance in hell of getting that right.

lines.speaker: dasher
lines.text: You need a lift? I'll give you a lift. Up you go. One, two...
lines.spoken: You need a lift? - I'll give you a lift. - Up you go. --- One, two ---

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Three?
lines.spoken: Three?

lines.speaker: dasher
lines.text: Four! I always skip three. It slows me down!
lines.spoken: Four! - I always skip three. --- It slows me down!

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: He didn't lift me. He threw me. I went up past the scoreboard, saw the whole North Pole, and came down on the scoreboard. Close enough.
lines.spoken: He didn't lift me. -- He threw me. -- I went up past the scoreboard, saw the whole North Pole, and came down on the scoreboard. ---- Close enough.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Hanging from the scoreboard, a gym bag. Scorched along the bottom. It smelled like a campfire wearing perfume.
lines.spoken: Hanging from the scoreboard, a gym bag. -- Scorched along the bottom. ---- It smelled like a campfire wearing perfume.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: There was a tag on the handle. 'If found, please return to C. The Ember Arms, Apartment Nine.'
lines.spoken: There was a tag on the handle. -- 'If found, please return to C. ---- The Ember Arms, Apartment Nine.'

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: C. That letter again. Following me around like a bad penny. A burning penny.
lines.spoken: C. -- That letter again. -- Following me around like a bad penny. ---- A burning penny.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Somewhere out there, somebody named C. was missing their gym bag. Their spare leg warmers. Maybe their dignity.
lines.spoken: Somewhere out there, somebody named C. was missing their gym bag. -- Their spare leg warmers. ---- Maybe their dignity.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: A lesser detective would turn it in to lost and found. I'm not a lesser detective. I'm a shorter one.
lines.spoken: A lesser detective would turn it in to lost and found. -- I'm not a lesser detective. ---- I'm a shorter one.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I'd return it personally. The Ember Arms. Apartment Nine. Purely professional.
lines.spoken: I'd return it personally. -- The Ember Arms. -- Apartment Nine. ---- Purely professional.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Wear a hat, dear! It's cold out!
lines.spoken: Wear a hat, dear! - It's cold out!

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: It was. For now.
lines.spoken: It was. --- For now.
